entry.title: Switch python-utils submodule URL from SSH to HTTPS
entry.content:
Switch python-utils submodule URL from SSH to HTTPS

SSH URLs in a tracked .gitmodules block anonymous clones of this public
repo. HTTPS works for strangers with no GitHub SSH key, and contributors
who prefer SSH can add a url.insteadOf rewrite in their own global
gitconfig without touching the tracked file.

entry.title: fix(managed-note-types): render feedback marker as inline SVG, pin z-…
entry.content:
fix(managed-note-types): render feedback marker as inline SVG, pin z-index

Emoji glyphs depend on the host having a color-emoji font, which Anki's bundled
Qt WebEngine often lacks on Linux (renders as a tofu box). Inline SVG needs no
font and no media file, so it's self-contained and device-independent like the
rest of the injector.

Also pins z-index explicitly: position:fixed alone only happened to float on
top because nothing else in Production's CSS used position — not guaranteed
once more managed fragments or hand-authored positioned elements show up.

entry.title: feat(managed-note-types): red-apple feedback marker via deterministic…
entry.content:
feat(managed-note-types): red-apple feedback marker via deterministic styling injection

Renders a small apple on cards whose user_feedback field is populated, so users
stop opening the edit window just to discover they already left feedback. The
RED/GREEN flag mechanics in feedback.py/edits.py are untouched — this is a
render-only visual substitute for checking the flag by hand.

Enrichment is a deterministic sentinel-block injector (styling_infrastructure/),
not an LLM call: stamping a known fragment into CSS/templates is closed-form and
idempotent, so an LLM would only add nondeterminism and corruption risk. Isolated
in its own package/tests dir ahead of the anticipated unified test-approach
refactor for this MCP.

entry.title: feat(feedback): working prototype of the deterministic feedback pipeline
entry.content:
feat(feedback): working prototype of the deterministic feedback pipeline

Package process-user-feedback-on-deck as a chain of deterministic Python
steps with a single LLM call, replacing the edit-card-batch fork.

- edit.py: new Edit step. Drives a fresh 'claude -p' (utils.call_isolated,
  prompt over stdin) to apply each card's user_feedback, returning changed
  fields as JSON on stdout. Python validates against the input note_ids,
  strips fences, and retries once before failing non-zero. No Write-tool
  call means no file-overwrite permission prompt and no spawn-time staleness.
- Remove edit-card-batch skill and dump-input.py: the pre-seed-output dance
  backfired (an existing file turned the creation prompt into an overwrite
  prompt) and is no longer needed.
- confirm.py / reset-test-deck.py: deterministic diff-print and standalone
  test fixture.
- Align the wire shape on 'fields' (was 'new_fields') across feedback.py,
  edits.py, and the batch tool.
- gitignore .artifacts/ (in-tree pipeline handoff files).
- Archive the initial design docs under initial-conceptions-and-aspirations/.

Verified end-to-end on zz-test-feedback: extract -> edit -> confirm -> apply
runs prompt-free, edits are reductive and correct, and the skip branch
retains a skipped card's pending feedback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: refactor(feedback): move extract_feedback and update_note_fields_batc…
entry.content:
refactor(feedback): move extract_feedback and update_note_fields_batch off the MCP tool list

Both had exactly one caller (this skill) and sat in every session's tool list for no
benefit. extract_feedback_records() and update_note_fields_batch() are now plain
functions, exposed to the pipeline via two new skill-local CLI scripts
(extract.py, apply.py) instead of @mcp.tool(). update_note_fields stays a tool —
it's useful ad hoc, outside the pipeline.

The record payload between Extract/Edit/Apply now passes through two static files
under /tmp instead of round-tripping through the orchestrator's and fork's context,
removing an LLM copy-drift vector. apply.py also now owns clearing user_feedback
deterministically (applying == processed), so edit-card-batch no longer has to
remember to emit it.

feedback.py moves out of managed_note_types/tools/ since it no longer registers any
MCP tools.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: feat(managed-note-types): diff-inside-write semantics + batch update …
entry.content:
feat(managed-note-types): diff-inside-write semantics + batch update tool

update_note_fields now accepts any subset of a note's fields — including all
of them — and filters to only actually-changed values before writing or
logging, rather than trusting the caller to pre-diff. This lets an LLM caller
(e.g. edit-card) round-trip full field dicts without polluting the log with
old==new entries or spuriously flipping the flag.

Adds update_note_fields_batch: loops the same logic over a list of updates,
continuing past per-note failures and returning a per-note changed/error
report instead of aborting the whole batch.

Also fixes a pre-existing bug: notesInfo returns [{}] (not []) for an unknown
note_id, so the old `if not info` check never caught missing notes — it fell
through to a KeyError on info[0]["fields"] instead of a clean ValueError.

Verified live against Anki: unchanged fields dropped from diff and log,
pure no-op calls write nothing, batch continues past a bad note_id, and the
bad-note_id case now raises a clean "not found" error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
